quickSummary: Fungi are classified into Phycomycetes (coenocytic), Ascomycetes (8 endogenous ascospores in asci), Basidiomycetes (4 exogenous basidiospores on sterigmata, 5 Puccinia stages), and Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi lacking known teleomorphs).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary Box
summaryBox.takeaway: Fungi are divided into four major classes based on mycelial septation, fruiting body architecture, and sexual spore origin (endogenous vs exogenous).

conceptBreakdown.content: Systematic fungal classification categorizes Kingdom Fungi into four major classes based on mycelial morphology, sexual spore development, and fruiting body architecture.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Phycomycetes (Lower Fungi: Oomycetes & Zygomycetes)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Phycomycetes (Lower Fungi: Oomycetes & Zygomycetes)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Characterized by a coenocytic, aseptate mycelium.

A. Oomycetes (Water Molds & Downy Mildews):
• Distinguishing Traits: Cell wall composed of cellulose and glucans (lacks chitin).
• Asexual Reproduction: Produces heterokont biflagellate zoospores (one anterior tinsel flagellum, one posterior whiplash flagellum).
• Sexual Reproduction: Oogamous fusion producing thick-walled, resistant Oospores.
• Key Representatives: *Phytophthora infestans* (caused the catastrophic Irish Potato Famine of 1845), *Albugo candida* (causes White Rust of Crucifers).

B. Zygomycetes (Conjugating Fungi):
• Distinguishing Traits: Cell wall contains chitin. Asexual spores are non-motile aplanospores or sporangiospores formed endogenously inside sporangia.
• Sexual Reproduction: Conjugation of gametangia produces a thick-walled, resting Zygospore.
• Key Representatives: *Rhizopus stolonifer* (Black Bread Mold), *Mucor*.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Ascomycetes (Sac Fungi)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Ascomycetes (Sac Fungi)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ASCOMYCETE SPORE FORMATION
                      
  Karyogamy in Ascogenous Hypha ──► Zygote (2n) ──► MEIOSIS ──► 4 Haploid Nuclei (n)
                                                                     │
  8 Endogenous ASCOSPORES per Ascus ◄── MITOSIS (1 Round) ───────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
Characterized by a septate mycelium with simple septa and the production of sexual spores endogenously inside sac-like structures called Asci (singular: Ascus).

• Spore Profiles:
- Asexual Spores: Conidia, produced exogenously on specialized conidiophores.
- Sexual Spores: Ascospores, produced endogenously inside the ascus. A standard ascus contains 8 ascospores (1 meiosis followed by 1 mitosis).

• Types of Fruiting Bodies (Ascocarps):
1. Cleistothecium: Completely closed, spherical ascocarp (*Erysiphe*).
2. Perithecium: Flask-shaped ascocarp with a narrow terminal pore (ostiole) (*Neurospora*, *Claviceps*).
3. Apothecium: Open, cup-shaped or saucer-shaped ascocarp exposing the hymenium (*Peziza*, Morels).

• Key Representatives:
- *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*: Unicellular yeast; reproduces by budding; baking/brewing.
- *Neurospora crassa*: 'Drosophila of Plant Genetics' (Beadle and Tatum's 'One Gene–One Enzyme' model).
- *Claviceps purpurea*: Causes Ergot of Rye; source of LSD (Lysergic Acid Diethylamide).
- *Penicillium chrysogenum*: Source of Penicillin.
- *Aspergillus flavus*: Produces carcinogenic Aflatoxins in stored grains.
- *Morchella* (Morels) and *Tuber* (Truffles): Gourmet edible delicacies.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.3 Basidiomycetes (Club Fungi)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.3 Basidiomycetes (Club Fungi)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE FIVE SPORE STAGES OF PUCCINIA
                        
  Stage 0: Pycniospores (Spermatia) ──► On Alternate Host (Barberry - Berberis)
  Stage I: Aeciospores               ──► Transferred from Barberry to Wheat
  Stage II: Urediniospores          ──► Repeats on Primary Host (Wheat - Summer)
  Stage III: Teliospores            ──► Resting Overwintering Stage (Wheat - Autumn)
  Stage IV: Basidiospores           ──► Produced in Soil; Infects Barberry
conceptBreakdown.content:
Includes mushrooms, bracket fungi, puffballs, rusts, and smuts. Possess septate mycelia with dolipore septa and clamp connections.

• Mycelial Stages:
1. Primary Mycelium: Monokaryotic (n), short-lived.
2. Secondary Mycelium: Dikaryotic (n+n), dominant vegetative body formed via Somatogamy.

• Spore Profiles:
- Asexual Spores: Generally absent.
- Sexual Spores: Basidiospores, produced exogenously on sterigmata on the exterior surface of a club-shaped Basidium (4 basidiospores per basidium).

• Key Representatives:
- *Agaricus bisporus*: Common edible mushroom.
- *Amanita phalloides*: 'Death Cap'; produces lethal amanitins (RNA polymerase II inhibitors).
- *Ustilago nuda / U. maydis*: Causes Loose Smut of wheat/corn.
- *Puccinia graminis tritici*: Causes Black Rust of Wheat across 5 macrocyclic spore stages.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.4 Deuteromycetes (Fungi Imperfecti)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.4 Deuteromycetes (Fungi Imperfecti)
conceptBreakdown.content:
An artificial, provisional grouping of fungi in which only the asexual or vegetative phases (Anamorph) are known.

• Teleomorph Reassignment: When the sexual stage (Teleomorph) is discovered through genetic analysis, the species is reassigned to either Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.
• Reproduction: Exclusively asexual via Conidia. Mycelium is septate and branched.
• Key Representatives:
- *Alternaria solani*: Causes Early Blight of Potato (target-board concentric leaf rings).
- *Colletotrichum falcatum*: Causes Red Rot of Sugarcane.
- *Trichoderma*: Free-living soil fungus used as a biological control agent against plant pathogens; source of the immunosuppressant Cyclosporin A.
